quote: Our interest lies in textual data, specifically, a method for how to generate a large training corpus in Runyankore... We used generation patterns to handle the phrasal structure...
...we generated one million Runyankore sentences, both labelled and unlabelled, from a dictionary of terms categorized into their appropriate parts of speech...

We found the use of a combined semantic and syntactic, pattern and grammar-based approach sufficient to generate one million Runyankore sentences, both labelled and unlabelled, from a dictionary of terms categorized into their appropriate parts of speech.
outputs: One million synthetic Runyankore sentences (labelled and unlabelled) covering multiple tenses, extensions, and sentiment variations.

quote: We evaluated for the quality of the generated text using a task-based evaluation, where we applied the generated text to some supervised and unsupervised machine learning tasks... We used FastText to obtain word vectors and assess the semantic relatedness from the generated text...

...we used FastText to obtain word vectors and assess the semantic relatedness from the generated text. We also trained and tested a sentiment analysis text classifier ... achieved 64% accuracy ... 77.3% accuracy...

The four-sentiment model was trained on 800,000 sentences and tested on 200,000 sentences, and achieved 64% accuracy. The binary sentiment model had a dataset with 541,751 examples, and it was trained on 500,000 sentences and tested on 41,751 sentences, and achieved 77.3% accuracy.
automatic_metrics: Semantic similarity via FastText nearest neighbor
